description: Controlled vocabularies for the OpenSpecLib Format v1. Normative. Values are case-sensitive.

quantity.reflectance: Ratio of reflected to incident radiation, or a reflectance factor (ratio to an ideal Lambertian reflector under the same geometry). Which of the two is determined by `geometry`. Dimensionless; nominal range 0 to 1, and reflectance factors may exceed 1.
quantity.transmittance: Ratio of transmitted to incident radiation. Dimensionless; nominal range 0 to 1.
quantity.emissivity: Ratio of emitted radiance to that of a blackbody at the same temperature. Dimensionless; nominal range 0 to 1.
quantity.absorbance: Decadic absorbance A = log10(1/x), where x is the reflectance or transmittance it was derived from. The basis SHOULD be recorded in `measurement_processing` (e.g. "absorbance_from_reflectance").

geometry.bidirectional: Directional illumination and directional view (BRF/BRDF; Schaepman-Strub et al. 2006, case 1). Goniometric or near-collimated measurements with stated illumination and viewing angles. Older libraries also use the word for laboratory lamp-and-probe setups; those are `biconical`.
geometry.biconical: Conical illumination and conical view (BCRF; case 5). Laboratory measurements with a lamp and a fore-optic, contact probe, leaf clip or FTIR reflectance attachment, including those that older libraries call 'bidirectional'.
geometry.directional_hemispherical: Directional illumination, hemispherical collection (DHR, 'black-sky albedo'; case 3). Laboratory spectrometers with an integrating sphere.
geometry.hemispherical_directional: Hemispherical illumination, directional view (HDRF; case 7). Field measurements under sky illumination with a narrow field of view.
geometry.hemispherical_conical: Hemispherical illumination, conical view (HCRF; case 8). Field spectroradiometer measurements under sky illumination with a fore-optic.
geometry.bihemispherical: Hemispherical illumination and hemispherical collection (BHR; case 9). Under isotropic illumination this is the 'white-sky albedo'. Also used for laboratory measurements of rock surfaces placed directly over an integrating-sphere port when the source describes them as BHR.
geometry.directional: Directional quantity without an illumination geometry, e.g. directional emissivity.
geometry.unknown: The source does not state the geometry. Use this rather than guessing.

wavelength_unit.cm-1: Reciprocal centimetres (wavenumber). Axes in cm-1 are usually stored in ascending wavenumber order, which is descending wavelength.

material_category.mineral: A single mineral species or mineral group.
material_category.rock: A rock: an aggregate of minerals.
material_category.soil: Soil or regolith, including soil horizons.
material_category.vegetation: Living or fresh plant material: leaves, canopies, flowers.
material_category.npv: Non-photosynthetic vegetation: dry plant matter, bark, wood, litter.
material_category.water: Liquid water bodies or water samples.
material_category.man_made: Manufactured materials: paints, plastics, building materials, fabrics.
material_category.lunar: Lunar samples, including returned regolith and rocks.
material_category.mixture: Physical, synthetic or simulated mixtures of materials from different categories.
material_category.other: Anything not covered above. Use `material_subcategory` to say what it is.

extension.material: Additional material description: subcategory, formula, keywords.
extension.bandpass: Per-band spectral bandpass (full width at half maximum).
extension.uncertainty: Per-band standard deviation of the values.

inclusion.complete: The collection contains every spectrum the source publishes.
inclusion.subset: The collection deliberately contains a subset of the source. `inclusion_notes` MUST say how it was chosen.
